Kuvitus: rullalautailija skeittiparkissa: Illustration: a skateboarder in a skatepark. The skateboarder is drawn in three places: on level ground in front of the ramp a long blue speed arrow v starts from her, three quarters of the way up the ramp the arrow is half as long, v/2, and at the top she is still for a moment, v = 0. A height gauge on the side of the ramp shows the heights: half of the speed is used up in the rise of three quarters, 3/4 h, the other half only in the last quarter, 1/4 h. The lengths of the arrows (2 : 1 : 0) and the heights are to scale.
Kaksi kuvaa samasta rampista, korkeudet: Two pictures of the same ramp, heights and speed arrows to scale. On the left a cart starts from the foot of the ramp at speed v, shown by a short blue arrow, and rises to height h. On the right the same cart starts at double the speed 2v, the arrow is twice as long, and it rises to height 4h, that is, four times as high. There is no friction.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa. Kolme reitt: Schematic picture, not to scale. Three routes from the same height h to the floor: on the left a ball falls straight down beside a tower, in the middle a cart goes down a steep ramp and on the right down a gentler ramp. There is no friction or air resistance. At the bottom all three have a blue speed arrow of equal length: the speed is the same, because gravitational potential energy depends only on height, not on the path.
Kaavakuva, korkeudet mittakaavassa. Vase: Schematic picture, heights to scale. On the left a wall shelf at a height of 1.80 metres and a table at a height of 0.80 metres from the floor, and on the shelf there is a book of 0.50 kilograms. On the right two vertical scales of potential energy values. When the zero level is the floor, the potential energy of the book is 8.8 joules on the shelf, 3.9 joules on the table and zero on the floor. When the zero level is the surface of the table, the values are 4.9 joules, zero and minus 3.9 joules. In both, the potential energy decreases by 4.9 joules when the book is moved from the shelf to the table.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: vaaka-akselilla n: Graph to scale: on the horizontal axis the speed from zero to 4.5 metres per second, on the vertical axis the kinetic energy from zero to 9 joules for an object whose mass is 1.0 kilograms. The graph is a parabola curving upward. At a speed of 2.0 metres per second the kinetic energy is 2.0 joules and at a speed of 4.0 metres per second 8.0 joules: double the speed gives four times the kinetic energy. Dashed lines show the readings.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: vaaka-akselilla p: Graph to scale: on the horizontal axis the speed of the ball from zero to 6 metres per second, on the vertical axis the kinetic energy of the ball from zero to 10 joules at intervals of one joule. The graph is a curve rising upward from the origin that passes through the points (2.0 m/s; 1.0 J), (4.0 m/s; 4.0 J) and (6.0 m/s; 9.0 J). The mass is not marked.
